name: Anterior meniscofemoral lig. (Humphry)
description: Anterior meniscofemoral ligament: an inconstant band from the lateral meniscus posterior horn, in front of the PCL, to the medial femoral condyle. On sagittal images a small low-signal focus or bulge directly in front of the PCL; thin, about 1.5–2 mm.

normal_values.thickness: about 1.5 mm in cadavers; 1–3 mm on MRI

variants_pitfalls: Present in about half to three-quarters of cadaver knees but seen on only about a third of MRIs (about half at 3 T), so not seeing it is normal.

It can mimic the double PCL sign. It is far smaller than the PCL, hugs it and traces to the lateral meniscus; a bucket-handle fragment is thicker, with a missing bow tie and a truncated medial meniscus.
Its insertion makes a pseudotear close to the PCL (on average about 1 image lateral to it in intact menisci); an apparent attachment 4 or more 3 mm images lateral raises the possibility of a tear.
The rare oblique meniscomeniscal ligament (about 1–4%) also crosses near the PCL but runs from the anterior horn of one meniscus to the posterior horn of the other.
